elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or minimum-volume commitment, including any minimum-spend or take-or-pay obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 states that Customer purchases “no minimum quantity” and has no take-or-pay obligation. Section 12.3 independently confirms that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment.

elements.element: Customer is liable for fees only for Services it actually uses or orders.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 places purchases on a “usage or ordered basis” and excludes any take-or-pay obligation, so payment is tied to usage or ordered Services rather than a minimum commitment.

elements.element: If a minimum purchase commitment exists, it applies only to the current term and not to any renewal or future term.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: Sections 2.1 and 12.3 eliminate any minimum purchase or minimum-volume commitment, so no commitment extends into any term.

elements.element: Any term covered by a minimum purchase commitment is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because there is no minimum purchase commitment covering any term. The residual reference to the next three years does not impose a minimum during those years.

elements.element: If a minimum purchase commitment exists, Customer may reduce its amount by notice.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: Customer has no minimum commitment to reduce.

elements.element: The notice period required for a reduction is no more than 30 days.
elements.evidence: No minimum commitment or reduction procedure exists, so no notice period exceeding 30 days can apply.

elements.element: If Customer has a commitment shortfall, the contractual remedy is a true-up.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the clause creates no commitment against which a shortfall could arise.

elements.element: A commitment shortfall does not trigger a penalty.
elements.evidence: There can be no commitment shortfall because no minimum commitment exists, and Section 2.1 expressly removes the take-or-pay obligation.

result.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position by eliminating both the minimum quantity and take-or-pay obligation and tying purchases to usage or ordered Services. Because no commitment remains, the fallback safeguards are satisfied conditionally rather than through express 12-month, reduction, notice, and true-up mechanics. The revision is limited to the offending commitment and does not disturb Section 12.3 or unrelated restrictions. Drafting quality is reduced by the awkward and unnecessary formulation “commits to purchase no minimum quantity ... in each of the next three years,” which could have been stated more directly.
